li_attr.description:
"Pre-Condition:
External Displays to Cover:  
HD Monitors /TVs (1920x1080)
Low resolution Monitors/TVs  (< 1920x1080)
High resolution Monitors/TVs ( > 1920x1080 Including 4k)
UDL (USB Connected) display.


Applicable External display ports: 
Type C Display port -  Cover TypeC -> (TypeC/HDMI/DP/DVI/VGA)
HDMI  Display port -  Cover HDMI -> (HDMI/DP/DVI/VGA)
DP Display  port -  Cover DP -> (HDMI/DP/DVI/VGA)
USB A(2.0/3.0)  for UDL

Note for Boxes : 
Use two monitors for boxes. One is treated as a primary display and the second one  is treated as an extended display.
For CHROMEBOX type
Close lid/ Open lid should be skipped.
One external display should be plugged in advance to act as onboard screen


*Basic test applies to FSI  and Sanity testing.
*Advanced test applies to Full-regression and Full-release testing.
*Suspend: Open crosh(Ctrl +Alt + t) - >  run command 'shell' -> run 'powerd_dbus_suspend'.
*Resume: Press any key / Mouse click / Press power button for 1second.
*Display-Related Persistent Notifications are removed M79. 
*Notifications are displayed for plug, unplug and mode change only until M78 (crbug.com/1008696)
*Test all available ports and including adapters/docks


Procedure:

-----------Sanity/FSI--------------------
Basic Testing :     
1. Boot and sign-in - Plug - Unplug 
-- [Plug] Display should extend to the last connected monitor/TV.
-- [Unplug] External monitor/TV should be disconnected.

2. Plug - Suspend - Resume - Unplug
--  [Plug] Display should extend to the last connected monitor/TV.
-- [Suspend] The device should be suspended and the monitor goes blank.
-- [Resume] The device resumes and external monitor comes up in extended mode.
-- [Unplug] External monitor/TV should be disconnected.

3. Boot and ising in  - Plug - Close lid - Open lid
-- [Plug] External display should be in extended mode.
-- [Close lid] Onboard screen should switch to external display.
-- [Open lid] Primary screen should switch back to internal display and external display should become extended display. 

 4. Switch between mirrored & extended modes (use keys or settings)
     Key combination: Ctrl + F4
     Settings flag: Settings -> Displays -> Mirro Internal Display (Enable/Disable)
-- User should be able to switch between mirror and extended modes using keys and and settings flag.
 
5. Switch between primary & extended.(use keys or settings)
    Key combination: Alt+ F4
    Settings flag: Settings -> Displays -> Extended display -> Screen  (change as Primary Display)
--External display should become primary and onboard should be changed as extended display.


--------- FullRelease/FullRegression-----------------
                                                                        
Advanced Testing: 
6. Boot and sign in - Plug - Suspend - Resume
-- [Plug] External display should be in extended mode.
-- [Suspend] The device should be suspended and the monitor goes blank.
-- [Resume] Both primary and extended monitors should work properly.

7. Unplug - Suspend - Plug - Resume
-- [Unplug] External display should be disconnected.
-- [Plug] Should not change anything in suspend state.
-- [Resume] Device display should  become primary  and external display should become extended.

8. Suspend - Unplug - Resume - Plug
-- [Suspend] The device should be suspended and the monitor goes blank.
-- [Unplug] Unplug should not change anything in suspend state.
-- [Resume] Device should display external monitor disconnected.
-- [Plug] External display should become extended.

9. Power off - Plug - Boot and sign in - Close lid - Unplug - Open lid -Plug.
-- [Boot and sing in ] External display should become extended soon after boot and during sign-in.
-- [Close lid] Primary screen switch to external display.
-- [Unplug] Device should enter into suspend state.
   (It may take some time up to 30 seconds)
-- [Open lid] Device should resume back.
-- [Plug] Display should extend to the last connected monitor/TV.

10. Plug - lock - Unplug -  Plug - login.
-- [Plug] External display should become extended.
 -- [Lock] Primary display should display lock screen and external display should display extended screen.
--[Unplug] External display should be disconnected. 
-- [Plug] External display should become extended.

11. Unified mode: Enable Unified desktop mode flag from about:flags
Connect multiple external displays to the device.
-- All monitors should act as single monitor.
-- [Plug/Unplug] Automatically resizes the unified display size.

  "

li_attr.description:
"Pre-Condition:
External Displays to Cover:  
HD Monitors /TVs (1920x1080)
Low resolution Monitors/TVs  (< 1920x1080)
High resolution Monitors/TVs ( > 1920x1080 Including 4k)
UDL (USB Connected) display.


Applicable External display ports: 
Type C Display port -  Cover TypeC -> (TypeC/HDMI/DP/DVI/VGA)
HDMI  Display port -  Cover HDMI -> (HDMI/DP/DVI/VGA)
DP Display  port -  Cover DP -> (HDMI/DP/DVI/VGA)
USB A(2.0/3.0)  

*Basic test applies to FSI  and Sanity testing.
*Advanced test applies to Full-regression and Full-release testing.
*Suspend: Open crosh(Ctrl +Alt + t) - >  run command 'shell' -> run 'sudo powerd_dbus_suspend'.
*Notifications are displayed for plug, unplug and mode change only until M78 (crbug.com/1008696)

*Test device types: Convertibles, Detachables and Slates/Tablets.
*For tablet mode by default external display enters into mirror mode.
*Test all available ports and including adapters/docks


Procedure:
--------------FSI/Sanity------------------
Basic Testing:  
1. Boot and sign in - Plug - Unplug - REM Sleep (only for Slate/Tablet) - Plug - Resume.
--[Plug] External display should come up with mirror mode.
--[Unplug] External display should be disconnected.
--[REM Sleep]  Device should enter into REM Sleep mode with short press of power button.
--[Plug] Plug should not change anything in REM Sleep mode.
--[Resume] Both device and external display should come up with mirror mode.
                        
                       
---------------FullRelease/FullRegression------------------
                                                                        
Advanced Testing:
2. Plug - Boot and sign in - Suspend - Resume
--[Boot and sign in] Both device and external display should be in mirror mode.
--[Suspend] The device should be suspended and the monitor goes blank.
--[Resume] Both device and external display should come up in mirror mode.

3. Unplug - Suspend - Plug - Resume
--[Unplug] External display should be disconnected.
--[Suspend Device should enter into suspend state.
--[Plug] External display should not change anything in suspend state.
--[Resume] Both device and external display should come up in mirror mode.

4. Suspend - Unplug - Resume - Plug
--[Suspend] Device should enter into suspend state.
--[Unplug] Unplug external display should not change anything in suspend state.
--[Resume] External display should be disconnected.
---[Plug] Both device and external display should enter into mirror mode.

 5. Plug - lock - Unplug -  Plug - Login.
--[Plug] Both device and external display should be in mirror mode.
--[Lock] Lock screen should be displayed on both displays.
--[Unplug] External display should be disconnected.
--[Plug] Lock screen should be displayed on both displays.
--[Login] Chrome OS should work properly.

6. Change orientation of the device.
--[Orientation] External display should follow the device display orientation.

7. Switch between Mirror and Extended mode ( use keyboard or Setting/Device/Displays)
  Key combination: Ctrl + F4 (Use USB keyboard)
  Settings/Device/Displays (Mirror mode) (Enable/Disable)
-- User should be able to switch between mirror and extended modes 
(Keep the device in extended mode and perform step 7)

8. Switch between primary and extended mode. (use keyboard or Setting/Device/Displays)
 Key combination: Alt+ F4 (Use USB keyboard)
 Settings/Device/Displays (Extended mode) (change as Primary Display)
-- Now external display should be changed as primary and primary should be changed as extended display.

9. Switch between tablet mode & clamshell mode
(Only for convertibles & detachables.)
-- Clamshell mode default mode is extended mode.
-- Tablet mode default mode is mirror mode.
-- Switching between tablet mode & clamshell should switch the display  between mirror 
  "

Basic Testing:
1. Plug M1 & M2 - Boot  and sign in - Close lid - Open lid.

--[Plug M1] M1 should come up in extended mode.

li_attr.author: sontis
li_attr.description:
"Objective
Verify the ability to have a single app span multiple displays

Related bugs:
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=511477
https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=520128

External monitors supported:
- Any monitor via HDMI/DP/DVI/VGA port  
- USB display  

Precondition
Unified Desktop is enabled from chrome://flags.

Procedure
1. Sign in and launch a browser in maximized window. 

2. Connect to any external monitor. 
__ Verify the single browser page spans over internal and external display.
__ No flickering, no crash.

3. Turn off and on "Allow windows to span displays" at chrome://settings/display. 
__ Verified Unified Desktop option can be turned off and on. 

4. Arrange monitor order at chrome://settings/display by dragging display box to different position. 
__ Verify monitor order is correct as arranged. 
__ No flickering, no cras.

5. Change Resolution at chrome://settings/display.  
__ No flickering, no crash. 

6. Enter to dock mode by close/open lid. 
__ No flickering, no crash. 

7. Suspend and resume the device by running 'powerd_dbus_suspend".
__ No flickering, no crash. 

8. Press Ctr-F4 to switch to mirror mode, and back to Unified view. 
__ Verify mirror mode works.
__ No flickering, no crash.

9. Add one more external display (2+ monitors) and repeat 3-8. 

10. Repeat 3-8 in Tablet mode. 

11. Repeat 3-8 against any ARC++ app which allows full screen. 
  "

li_attr.author: sontis
li_attr.description:
"Introduced with crbug.com/790723

Per Test review bug crbug.com/794413 instructions:
 - Changing display size should keep things sharp. No picture quality deterioration.
 - At any given display size none of the bugs mentioned in this umbrella bug should be noticed: crbug.com/731293
 - The system should be usable to the extent that the user can change the display size. It should not become so zoomed in that the user cannot select options, or so small that the user is unable to see any option.
 - The display should not go blank or dark at any display size setting.
 - The display size setting for a given display should persist across system shutdown.    -- https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=794413#c9
 - When the resolution of a display is changed, the display size that the user had selected in the past for this new resolution should be loaded. 
 - The display size corresponding to each resolution should persist across system restart. 
 - Everything should work as expected at any display size. That is mouse clicks, display rotation, overscan setting, touch calibration etc.
 - The keyboard shortcut of (CTRL, SHIFT, +/-) should change the display size of the display which houses the mouse pointer currently.
 - The resolution picked before updating from M-1 should be the same as the resolution shown in the "looks like" section of the display settings after updated to M (milestone). This should be true for all resolutions on the device.  This should be true for internal displays, external displays, 4k displays.



Pre-Condition:
    - External Display (HD, 4K, 8K)
    - CrOS DUT running R67 or later
    - Have the chromeos device on previous milestone, connect to specific external display and set specific resolution. Note this resolution down.


Procedure:

 1)  Connect an external display to the DUT.
 1.a)  Autoupdate to the current milestone and confirm same resolution('Looks like') is present for this specific display.

 - Display Size/Resolution should not be changed.

 2)  From Settings > Display, change the display size by dragging the slider.  Start with the slider all the way left (tiny) and progress towards the right (huge)

    - Changing display size should keep things sharp. No picture quality deterioration.  No pixel gaps between the UI and the display edges.
    - The system should be usable to the extent that the user can change the display size.  It should not become so zoomed in that the user cannot select options, or so small that the user is unable to see any option.
    - The display should not go blank or dark at any display size setting.
    - Everything should work as expected at any display size. That is mouse clicks, display rotation, overscan setting, touch calibration etc.

 3)  Use the keyboard shortcut of (CTRL, SHIFT, +/-) to increase or decrease the display size.  Now change the external display's resolution.  Once changed, switch the resolution back to default (100%).
  
    - The display size should increase and decrease when the keyboard shortcut is used.

 4)  With the external display still plugged in, restart the DUT.  Repeat Step #2.

    - Display Size/Resolution should not be changed.

 5)  Unplug and Replug the external display.  Repeat Step #2.

    - Display Size/Resolution should not be changed.
      
 6)  Convert the device into Tablet Mode and repeat the above steps in tablet mode.

 7) Switch to different display(HD, 4K, 8K) and repeat the steps 1 - 5
  "

Internal display (Primary)
External display (Extended)

__Now State:
Internal display (Primary) : Internal.window
External display (Extended): Monitor. window

__ External display window should switch between internal and external displays using previous window bounds.

li_attr.description:
"Precondition
1) Chromeos Device with USB type-c support (ex: Samus)
2) Multiport typeC adapter (i.e. Apple dongle).
3) Cables to connect external display ( ex: HDMI to HDMI)
4) USB Peripherals (USB stick, USB mouse, USB keyboard, USB webcam, USB head set)

Testing scenarios:
1. Hotplug the [non-powered] dongle alone
2. Power up the dongle
3. Hotplug peripheral(s) - one by one, or in combination - while dongle is plugged to chromeos device
4. Unplug and plug back the dongle while all peripherals are plugged to the dongle
4. Unplug, flip, and plug back the dongle while all peripherals are plugged to the dongle
5. Reboot the chromeos device with peripherals connected to the powered dongle.
6. Remove power from dongle and reboot chromeos device
7. Power up, Power down, and Power up again the dongle while all ports are busy with ExtDisplay and HID(kb, or mouse)
8. SUSPEND/RESUME 
8.1. Plug > Suspend > Resume.
8.2. Plug > Suspend > Unplug > Resume > Plug
8.3. Unplug > Suspend > Plug > Resume

Procedure 
Note: Cover all testing scenarios for the following conditions.

1)  Use the multi-port dongle(i.e. Apple adapter whith HDMI and USB-A ports)  and with power source(high- and low- voltage adapter)
 -- User should able to charge the chromeos device using the powered dongle 
 -- charging(high or low voltage) icon present(max 3 seconds to appear) when charging, and disappear(max 3 seconds) when power is disconnected(normal/discharging icon present instead).
 -- 'power_supply_info' output should be relevant.
 -- Peripherals should be functioning as expected in both powered and non-powered dongle screnario.

3) Check the peripherals discovery/mount/unmount times.
-- Mount/Unmount should not take longer than acceptable time.

9) Convert the device into Tablet Mode and repeat the above steps in tablet mode.
    Note: Onboard physical keyboard and Trackpad does not work in tablet mode.  "

li_attr.author: sontis
li_attr.description:
"Precondition
1) Chromeos Device with USB type-c support (ex: Samus)
2) USB Type-C multi-port docking station(i.e. HP Elite).
3) Cables to connect external display ( ex: HDMI to HDMI, DP to DP...)
4) All USB Peripherals (USB stick, USB mouse, USB keyboard, USB webcam, USB head set..)
5) Ethernet connection.
6) 3.5mm head set.

Testing scenarios:
1. Boot the device with dock connected
2. Hotplug the dock alone
3. Hotplug the dock while all peripherals are plugged to the dock
4. Hotplug peripheral(s) - one by one, or in combination - while docking station is plugged to chromeos device
5. Docking station only - Power up, Power down, and Up again the dock while all ports are busy with ExtDisplay and HID(kb, or mouse)
6. SUSPEND/RESUME 
6.1. Plug > Suspend > Resume.
6.2. Plug > Suspend > Unplug > Resume > Plug
6.3. Unplug > Suspend > Plug > Resume

Procedure 
Note: Cover all testing scenarios for the following steps.

1)  Use the multi-port docking station with peripheral ports used/plugged, with power source
 -- User should able to charge the chromeos device using powered dock station - charging icon present, 'power_supply_info' output.
 -- Peripherals should be functioning as expected

2) Confirm the docking station(i.e. HP Elite) as a power input. Use 'power_supply_info' to confirm power source.
 -- User should able to charge the chromeos device using dock station.

3) Check the Docking station mount/unmount times on USB storage.
-- Mount/Unmount should not take longer than acceptable time.

4) Use the docking station to connect the external display.
-- User should able to use all the display ports from docking station successfully.

5) Check Ethernet port on docking station.
-- Ethernet port should work and connect successfully.

6) Check all USB (2.0 and 3.0) ports available on docking station.
-- All the ports should work properly for the tested peripherals.

7) Check 3.5mm port.
-- 3.5mm port should work properly with the audio peripheral. 
[In most cases audio jack is presented as USB audio on chromeos device audio settings/uber menu]

8) Make sure you covered all the available ports on docking station.

9) Convert the device into Tablet Mode and repeat the above steps in tablet mode.
    Note: Onboard physical keyboard and trackpad does not work in tablet mode.  "
li_attr.goal: USB Type-C Multi-Port adapter and Docking station should work properly.
